title: Bolder hand: choose the visual world
question: Six foreign forms, fused with RQ's product. The catalogue wall leads by the roll. Pick one, steer, or re-roll again. Copy stays as written in every direction.

options.label: The Catalogue Wall
options.thesis: RQ's work arranged like a streaming home screen: the featured automation fills the billboard, and every row is something an office still does by hand.
materials: full-bleed authored tile artwork as the only colour
options.viewport: A full-bleed billboard with a live Three.js scene of the Outlook to Dropbox automation as its artwork. The headline sits as the title, with Contact us as the play button and What we build as more info. The first row of tiles peeks above the fold.
options.case: Every owner already knows how to use this layout, and it frames the case study as the featured title.
options.risk: The dark ground drifts toward dark tech and the entertainment register, and each tile needs real authored artwork or the wall looks empty.

raised.raise: The billboard artwork is a live WebGL scene driven by the pointer, not a still poster.
Tile states print themselves (for example, Running, or 1 click to archive) instead of using badges and chrome.
The focused row's lift is the only depth on the page; everything else stays flat.

options.label: Snap to System
options.thesis: Real photographs of real work, overrun by loud coloured bars that scatter and then snap to a hidden module: messy operations locked into a system.
materials: multiply overlaps that mix new colours
options.viewport: A tilted photograph under a stack of saturated bars that arrive scattered and lock to the grid. The headline is set inside one bar and Contact us is the yellow bar. The type is small and businesslike; the bars carry the volume.
options.case: It beats the lead on both axes: it reads as a confident, serious firm, and the scatter-then-snap motion shows the offer literally.
options.risk: It depends on real photography (the founders and the work). Without that it is just bars on grey, and the loud colour can fight the premium brief.

options.label: Below the Surface
options.lineage: technical deep dives down a volcanic wall
options.thesis: Scrolling is a descent: the manual work sits below the surface, and RQ goes down and finds it.
options.viewport: The headline sits over turquoise surface light, with a Geist Mono depth gauge reading 0 m down the left edge and Contact us at the surface. The thermocline band waits just below the fold.
options.case: It holds product clarity, because discovery-first becomes descending to where the manual work hides. It loses audience identification, because diving is foreign to most owners.
options.risk: It can turn into a long-scroll gimmick or a nature documentary, and the deep sections go dark.

options.label: Shader Portal
options.thesis: A full-screen living shader with thin type floating over it.
options.viewport: One huge word over breathing colour.
options.case: It fuses poorly: it hides the offer, and it is the dark awwwards-studio look the brief refuses.
options.kept: The hero artwork as a live WebGL scene.

options.label: Phosphor Terminal
options.thesis: The site as one scrolling transcript.
options.viewport: A blinking cursor and an 80-column field.
options.case: It fuses poorly: it is a developer's tool, not an owner's, and it repeats the current case study's terminal.
options.kept: States print themselves instead of using chrome.

options.label: Curved-Crease Shell
options.thesis: One curved crease turns a flat sheet into a rigid shell.
options.viewport: A cream disc lifting along a charcoal arc.
options.case: It fuses poorly: an abstract geometry lesson, set in the cream-and-italic-serif rut.
options.kept: One structural line owns the depth.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean light agency site: white ground, near-black type, one accent and product screenshots, executed at full craft.
canonCard.viewport: Split hero: headline and buttons on the left, a product visual on the right.
canonCard.risk: Close to the current build and indistinguishable from other agencies by design.
